nodes.title: SG-5 · Implement round lifecycle and admin API
nodes.body:
Context: the backend stores contributions as Markdown under worlds/<world>/rounds/<round>/contributions and has no round write model, scheduler or admin API. Desired behavior: a round model persisted in round.yaml with a transition table, open/close that freeze a snapshot.yaml and record the Git commit SHA, a clock-injected scheduler, and admin endpoints behind an admin token. Expected result: rounds move through the lifecycle only by legal transitions and admins can drive them over HTTP. Why: the Worker and the next-round cycle depend on a trustworthy round record.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a round in any status, when a transition not in the table is requested, then it is rejected with ErrIllegalTransition and round.yaml is unchanged
- Given an OPEN round, when it is closed, then snapshot.yaml is written once, the freeze commit SHA is recorded and status is CLOSED
- Given a frozen round, when a contribution is saved, then the store rejects it and no file is written
- Given a fake clock, when it passes starts_at or ends_at, then the scheduler opens or closes the round
- Given a request without or with a wrong admin token, when any admin endpoint is called, then the response is 401


## Scope
- In scope: backend/internal/round package
- In scope: Git HEAD lookup in gitrepo
- In scope: frozen guard in contribution FileStore
- In scope: admin middleware, round endpoints, execution endpoints
- In scope: config for admin token and round defaults
- Out of scope: Local Worker
- Out of scope: frontend admin UI
- Out of scope: release publishing
- Out of scope: changing the existing world current-round reader
- Preserve: existing contribution validation behaviour
- Preserve: player session endpoints
- Preserve: gitrepo Commit signature


## Technical constraints
- No database; state lives in YAML files committed through gitrepo.Committer
- Go 1.22, chi v5, yaml.v3, module github.com/worldseed/storyforge/backend
- Clock is injected, never time.Now directly in tested code


## Definition of done
- All six requirements implemented with unit tests passing via go test ./...


## Non-functional requirements
- Admin token compared in constant time


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Round model with 13 statuses, transition table and round.yaml store
nodes.body:
Context: world.Round only reads id/number/status/times. Desired behavior: a round package defines statuses SCHEDULED, OPEN, CLOSED, ANALYZING, PLANNING, DEVELOPING, TESTING, BUILDING, PUBLISHING, COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELLED, RECOVERING, a transition table, and a FileStore reading and writing worlds/<world>/rounds/<round-lowercase>/round.yaml. Expected result: illegal transitions are rejected. Why: single source of truth for the lifecycle.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given status SCHEDULED, when transitioning to OPEN, then it succeeds; to CLOSED it returns ErrIllegalTransition
- Given a saved round, when Get is called, then the same fields are returned including base_release and freeze_commit
- Given an unsafe world or round id, when Get or Save is called, then an error is returned and nothing is written


## Scope
- In scope: backend/internal/round/round.go

- Out of scope: open/close logic
- Out of scope: HTTP
- Preserve: worlds/<world>/rounds/<round>/ path convention used by contribution.FileStore

- Write via temp file then os.Rename


## Definition of done
- round package compiles with table and store


## Non-functional requirements
- Atomic writes

- None

nodes.title: REQ · Open and close rounds with frozen snapshot and recorded Git commit SHA
nodes.body:
Context: no code creates, opens or closes rounds. Desired behavior: Open records start/end (24h default) and base release; Close writes snapshot.yaml once listing contributions, commits it, records the exact SHA from the Git interface, sets CLOSED; frozen rounds reject new contribution files. Expected result: contribution snapshot is immutable. Why: the Worker needs a stable input.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a SCHEDULED round, when opened with no duration, then ends_at = starts_at + 24h and base_release is recorded
- Given an OPEN round, when closed, then snapshot.yaml lists its contributions, freeze_commit equals the SHA returned by Head, status is CLOSED
- Given snapshot.yaml exists, when FileStore.Save is called for that round, then ErrFrozen is returned and no file is created
- Given a round that is not OPEN, when closed, then ErrIllegalTransition is returned and no snapshot is written


## Scope
- In scope: round/lifecycle.go
- In scope: round/snapshot.go
- In scope: gitrepo Head
- In scope: contribution ListByRound and frozen guard
- Out of scope: scheduler
- Out of scope: HTTP
- Preserve: Committer.Commit behaviour
- Preserve: contribution Save semantics for open rounds


## Technical constraints
- snapshot written with O_EXCL and mode 0o444
- Git access only through the gitrepo interface


## Dependencies
- R1


## Definition of done
- Lifecycle service compiles


## Non-functional requirements
- Serialize lifecycle operations with a mutex


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Scheduler auto-opens and auto-closes rounds using an injected clock
nodes.body:
Context: nothing triggers open/close at scheduled times. Desired behavior: Scheduler.Tick uses an injected Clock to open SCHEDULED rounds whose starts_at has passed and close OPEN rounds whose ends_at has passed. Expected result: rounds change state without admin action. Why: continuous cycle.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a SCHEDULED round with starts_at <= clock now, when Tick runs, then Open is called
- Given an OPEN round with ends_at <= now, when Tick runs, then Close is called
- Given times in the future, when Tick runs, then nothing is called


## Scope
- In scope: backend/internal/round/scheduler.go
- Out of scope: process wiring
- Preserve: Service API


## Technical constraints
- Clock interface {Now() time.Time}


## Dependencies
- R2

nodes.title: REQ · Admin token middleware and round/admin configuration
nodes.body:
Context: no admin protection exists. Desired behavior: middleware requiring Authorization: Bearer <admin token> with constant-time comparison, failing closed when no token is configured; config gains admin.token (env STORYFORGE_ADMIN_TOKEN) and round.duration, base_release, scheduler_interval defaults. Expected result: admin routes are unreachable without the token.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given no Authorization header, when called, then 401 and next handler not run
- Given a wrong token, when called, then 401

- Given round config absent, when loaded, then duration is 24h, base_release 1.0.0, scheduler_interval 30s

- Out of scope: routes
- Preserve: existing config defaults and env overrides
